title: FACT CHECK: Photos of Duterte in the hospital are AI-generated
summary: The viral posts, claiming to show photos of a bedridden Duterte, circulated ahead of his ICC trial. No official reports confirm his alleged hospitalization.

blocks.text: Claim: Former president Rodrigo Duterte was taken to the hospital ahead of the start of his trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC), as shown in photos circulating online.
Why we fact-checked this: A collage of images depicting an individual resembling Duterte lying in a hospital bed has circulated on Facebook since November 24.

On November 25, Facebook user “Atty. Shiela Sison” shared the collage in a post that garnered 2,900 reactions, 926 comments, and 61 shares as of writing. The page “Sen. Rodante Marcoleta Supporters” posted it a day earlier, receiving 699 reactions, 126 comments, and 10 shares as of writing.
Both posts use the caption: “Get well soon po Tatay Digong sinugod sa hospital matapos…”
(Get well soon, Father Digong. Rushed to the hospital after…)

The caption did not specify the reason for Duterte’s alleged hospitalization. The phrase “See more” is also manually typed into the caption rather than generated by Facebook, and the collage is embedded in a link instead of an album.
Many commenters appear to have accepted the images as authentic, posting prayers and messages wishing Duterte a swift recovery.

The facts: The photos were generated using artificial intelligence. AI detection tools Hive Detect and Sightengine assessed the images as 99.5% and 87% likely to be AI-generated or deepfake content, respectively.

Duterte has been held at the ICC detention facility in The Hague, The Netherlands since his March 2025 arrest. Neither the ICC nor any credible news outlet has reported that he was transported to a hospital.
Duterte at the ICC: The misleading posts emerged shortly before Duterte’s trial, which is scheduled to begin on November 30.

Trial Chamber III will determine whether the former leader is guilty beyond reasonable doubt of murder and attempted murder as crimes against humanity, related to his anti-illegal drug campaign in Davao as mayor and vice mayor, allegedly carried out through the Davao Death Squad, and subsequently nationwide after he became president in 2016.

Prosecutors plan to present around 100 witnesses, with five expected to testify before the court recesses for the holidays on December 18. (READ: Here’s what to expect at the opening of Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC trial)

Supreme Court update: On November 24, the Supreme Court dismissed petitions questioning Duterte’s arrest. The High Court ruled that the petitions were moot because a writ of habeas corpus cannot be enforced beyond Philippine jurisdiction and Duterte is already in ICC custody. Nine justices voted to dismiss the petitions, while four dissented.

The Court clarified that the dismissal does not imply that Duterte’s arrest and transfer to The Hague were necessarily legal, and that any claims of rights violations must be pursued through other legal proceedings.
